Standing (I can't play N _and_ monitor this... well, I could, but I don't want to) CPU usage (mine's a PIII (E) 733MHz, 256mb ram, win me):
A - 63%
B - 58%
C - 54%
D - 60%
1.3c - 100%

On 30-1, which isn't a very power hungry level:
A - Smooth, a couple of tiny jerks.
B - Constant small choppiness
C - Pretty smooth, occasional choppiness
D - Occasional large jerks
1.3c - Often background chopiness

On 40-1:
A - A fair bit of jumping, definately still playable
B - A bit better than 30-1
C - Painfully jerky, a lot of constant lagging
D - About the same as 30-1 except there's often background chopiness
1.3c - Often background chopiness

Haven't tried it offline, which is when I normally play N, but these projectors actually seem okay for me.

#2876 1 2005-05-16T12:38:10Z astro
Firstly, it's for Windows, so all you Mac'ers can go elsewhere. Face it, you didn't get a Mac so you could run lots of programs. Anyway, this is NLO. You can split up all your user levels into seperate files (they all need to start with "&userdata=") and use NLO to edit them or switch them with the current userlevels.txt for use in N. In other words, you can keep different kinds of levels in seperate text files, which makes it a lot easier to maintain.

Yep, it's Visual Basic (needs VB6 runtimes), and I haven't bothered optimising it or anything, so it can take a few seconds, up to 1 min, to load big (200kb +) files (switching is near-instant). Oh, and you don't need to exit N to switch files, just click refresh list in N.

New version, you don't need waste time loading the files unless you want to edit themwhich really isn't advised, since a real text editor would be faster and gives you more flexibility.

#3691 1 2005-07-15T08:54:31Z astro
NB: This is hacking like the O'Reilly series of books, like Google Hacking.
Also, the forum system shortens the URLs, so hover over them to see them in full.

I discovered that you can combine all kinds of filters with NUMA to get exactly what you want, if you manuall append them onto the end of the url. I'm not sure how good I am at describing this, so here's an example:
http://numa.notdot.net/browse?sort=created...egory=4&count=5
That will display 5 of nevermore's race maps, in descending order from when they where created. If you add the favorites variable on, you can see 5 of nevermore's race maps in my favorites: http://numa.notdot.net/browse?sort=created...5&favorites=551
I've only got one, but you can see how it would work.

You can also use this to export userlevel.txt files, just change the browse? part into userlevels?, like: http://numa.notdot.net/userlevels?sort=rat...=desc&count=100 (the top 100 maps).

All the variables that you can use (as far as I know) are:
favorites
order (asc/desc)
sort (created/lastupdated/rating/votes/random)
author
count
name
category (0[all]/1[action]/2[puzzle]/3[test level]/4[race]/5[survival]/6[incomplete]/7[dda])

Hopefully y'all get that, if not, ask for clarification.

#84159 21 2005-07-17T08:33:17Z astro
He's in the middle of Part I because that's the first level. All subsequent ones follow on.

As for rule 2, if the first level looked like this (and thankfully, it doesn't):
| | x | x
x | | x |
x x | x |
| x x | |
x x | | |
The next level would look something like:
x | x | | 
| x | x |
| x | x x
x | | | x
x | x x x
Because the two columns on the far left on the first level go over to the far right on the other. If you were to join them together, it would scroll fluidly:
x | x | | x | x
| x | x | | x |
| x | x x | x |
x | | | x x | |
x | x x x | | |
My diagram is probably more confusing than anything, but it may help to illustrate it. Look at the existing levels for how it works.

Also, the typical Macintosh user's argument that's it's more secure, and immune from viruses in bugs is becoming less and less true. Macintosh users are that complacent about security that when something does happen, no-one will be protected. If you're smart with using a computer, the OS makes little difference to you getting security and viruses.

It also depends what you're using the computer for. The ease of use Windows provides as well as the wide variety of software is good for an average home user. #99457 59 2005-09-11T03:24:27Z astro
An invasion attempt does not necessarily mean someone is trying to put a virus or trojan onto your computer, only that it has been scanned. Generally the scans are looking for trojans that are already on your computer - they normally get there through email or internet downloads. That said, firewalls are important, especially for monitoring outbound traffic (potentially from a torjan). One thing that cannot be blamed on simply being connected to the internet without a firewall is viruses. There is no way anyone is just gonna magically drop a virus on your computer from the interweb without you accepting some kind of download.

NEVER, EVER put a CD or DVD in your microwave! They produce large amounts of extremely poisonous gas. PEOPLE HAVE DIED FROM THIS, even in large, well-ventilated rooms.

Furthermore, the explosion from some lighbulbs is powerful enough to drive shrapnel through the walls and blow the door off the microwave at a speed high enough to cause injury.

In fact, don't put anything that isn't food or a microwave-safe dish into your microwave. Pretty much everything else either sears your eyes out with UV radiation (helloooo, cataracts), explodes, or releases poisnonous gases. If you want to see pretty lights and explosions, go watch a fireworks show.

Tinfoil or any other light metal in your microwave (well, anything that isn't meant to explode, at least... a grenade certainly _would_ break it open) would not shower you with shrapnel, unless you are somehow using the microwave with the door open or you are standing inside it yourself. #106181 4 2005-10-07T14:49:38Z astro
There are two ways you can do it:
First, you need to jump into the trench. Just lightly tap jump so you flick the switch as well. Wait until the laser has stopped. Once the laser has stopped, run right and don't jump until the laser is just about to activate (you've got 1 second after it begins to power up). Jump over the laser drone. Run underneath the laser drone and out of that section. Grab the gold, jump up to get the switch, and drop down into the exit.

--or--
First, you need to jump into the trench. Just lightly tap jump so you flick the switch as well. Wait until the laser has stopped. Once the laser has stopped, jump out of the trench as high as possible so that the laser aims above you. Wait for it to stop, and jump over the laser drone. Run out of that section. Grab the gold, jump up to get the switch, and drop down into the exit.


The second way is probably easier, but the first is faster.

Where have you been, people? In the last week it has spread to Europe in a big way. Romania, Turkey, Greece, Croatia, and Sweden have gotten it, and as glenno said, a parrot with it died in customs.

Ever heard of the Spanish flu epidemic, where around 30 million people worldwide died? That was around 3% of the world population, and around 20% were affected by the flu in some way. Modern technology should help us fight this one, but in the end, if it mutates and the mutated virus begins spreading, we are well and truly f—ked.

The scare a few years back was largely confined to Asia and south-east Asia. Now it's really starting to spread, and I think the world really should be scared.

I've got a news alert going about it, and it is happening at an alarming rate now. The most recent thing is that Sweden has reported an incidence of bird flu, although they are unclear if it is the H5N1 strain. Russia has also reported a new case of it, a boy has become infected in Thailand, and Taiwan claim (you never know if it's just propaganda with the whole China-Taiwan thing) that they have discovered it in some birds coming from China.

Be alert, if not afraid.

Oh, and at iangb: a global pandemic of bird flu would be bad economically, because it would require the culling of millions of birds, and people who work with birds would become infected. The real fear is that it will mutate into a virus that can spread from humans to humans, something that has already happened in the past.

Do a search for "n_v14b_userdata.sol". This is where the data is stored, and on a windows computer it is usually in a directory like:
C:\WINDOWS\Application Data\Macromedia\Flash Player\#SharedObjects\ALF474WP\localhost
(if you're using Windows 95, 98, ME), or:
C:\Documents & Settings\username\Application Data\Macromedia\Flash Player\#SharedObjects\TSV434WQ\localhost

Quote: The Daily Llama, Nov 4 2005, 01:58 PM
Righto. Asked for my reasons for disliking John Howard is just asking for trouble... just a shame that this is eating into time that should be spent studying, so I'll have to be relatively brief...

1) The Children Overboard Scandal.
Well, it was a scandal. Involving Children. Who were overboard. Seriously, though, I reckon it should have affected John Howard a lot more than it did.

2) Refusing to say "sorry".
Okay, I understand the legal reasons behind it. I understand John Howard for this entirely. And, while I really can't blame him for it, it still adds to my violent dislike of him.

3) Licking George Bush's rear.
In World War 1 and 2, the messages rang something like "The Mothercountry, England, has gone to war. Thus, we must join them." And now he is doing the same, with America. All I reckon he's achieving by the whole joining Bush so... stupidly... with everything he does, (ESPECIALLY the war on Terror), is making Australia a bigger terrorist target.

4) The GST
Allright. The GST wasn't even that bad, from the perspective of- say- my family, which is most definately more wealthy than most. And a tax that... well... "equalises" things would be good, from our perspective.
But I do believe that the rich and more wealthy should cough up more tax than the less. And I do believe that paying 10% more for everything just sucks.
My main problem with the GST is, though, the fact that he is still pushing to introduce more taxes after this, despite what he originally said.

5) Old growth forest logging
This was just pathetic. Yeah, just chop it all down, screw everything else, as long as I keep the loggers happy, and short- term profit rolling in, everything else can GO TO HELL!!!!!
And don't even talk to me about his- *snigger*- "conservation" of, well, places that are allready pretty much inacessable to loggers.

6) Trodding on the right to free speech
Come on. I just mean, COME ON! I've allready talked about the new anti- terror laws... detaining people for expressing their opinoins? How can you justify that?
Detaining people in their houses, for up to two weeks, without even having to provide a reason? How on EARTH can they justify that?

7) Abusing his majority in the senate
What else can I say here? He has shown next- to- no reserve, leaving pretty much no time for debating legislations since he knows he's gonna get it anyway.

Okay, Labor sucks. They suck a lot. But, well, I strongly believe that it is the lesser of two evils. On one hand, they look like they could, potentially, hurt this nation. John Howard allready has, a lot.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

And there was more stuff, but really, I should do some more work, so I'm gonna head off now. Really. And I won't be returning for quite some time, really, I promise.

Cya on the flipside.

Firstly, at Atilla's post: Amen.

1) It did affect Howard. Positively. With that election, they got a boost in terms of their stance on border security. Then the crap hit the air conditioner, but 4 years is plenty of cooling down time. (AKA, I agree with you on that.)

2) I never get that. Sorry for what, exactly? It has nothing to do with this generation, nothing at all.

3) I suppose you are right with that. Still, I don't mind the idea of having an ally in America.

4) Not necessarily 10% more. It did replace many taxes - certainly, not as many as it should have, but some things went down (computers!).

6) Proposed new laws.

7) I wouldn't say it's abuse. The coalition won the senate -- won it by the rights of the people. I don't agree with one side having a senate majority, but I'm glad it is a coalition majority.

Clearly, I support the Liberals. I really think the major reforms our country has undergone are generally positive. Besides, Labor may have been just as bad. It has been 9 years since they last had power, it's hard to know.

#118379 62 2005-11-27T04:33:22Z astro
:: Low Bandwidth Ahead - Templex ::

[tileset fun] :: 22/30
The tileset definately makes this map what it is. The small, narrow paths are great for walljumping.

[object fun] :: 16/30
The mines are well placed, and the zap drones are decent, but it could do with something else. It was lacking the real drive to zip around.

[fun together] :: 22/30
Overall, it works. Nothing spectacular, but it's definately good.

[total] :: 60/90



:: Pixel Stream - Templex ::

[tileset fun] :: 23/30
A more complicated tileset than Low Bandwith Ahead, and it's a lot more fun. Faster, harder, funner.

[object fun] :: 22/30
The mines are very well placed, and the drones do a good job. The placement of gold and launchpads are also very succesful.

[fun together] :: 24/30
This definately works together. It's more challenging than LBA, but for me this was definately more fun. LBA was a walk in the park; Pixel Stream was a run in the park.

[total] :: 69/90



:: Creschful - blazeraid ::

[tileset fun] :: 19/30
If I could, I'd give this points for originality. It's not bad... it's got a flow to it, which is slightly interrupted by the wacky tileset. You can get some good speed and pull off a few good jumps.

[object fun] :: 17/30
Not much to say. Some good placement.

[fun together] :: 19/30
It's alright.

[total] :: 55/90



:: Speed City - Templex ::

[tileset fun] :: 18/30
Good flow and speed in many parts. Unfortunately, there are some parts that interupt the flow, and it's very linear.

[object fun] :: 15/30
THe floorchasers killed a lot of the flow for me. When you die like that, it isn't very fun.

[fun together] :: 18/30
When you're in a fast, flowing section, it's a fun map. When the tileset or floorchasers interrupt that flow, it becomes un-fun very fast.

[total] :: 51/90



:: Resilient Forest - Templex ::

[tileset fun] :: 21/30
Inventive tileset, but fun? Not really - it's a great tileset, but the restrictive movement doesn't do it for me.

[object fun] :: 18/30
Not much to speak of except gold, which was well-placed.

[fun together] :: 16/30
Doesn't do it for me.

[total] :: 55/90



:: Ominous - Blazeraid ::

[tileset fun] :: 23/30
Smooth and flowing. Everything's easy to get to, which is fun.

[object fun] :: 20/30
Decent placement, except for a couple of odd rockets. The gold is well placed, the enemies are a challenge, and the thwumps are fun.

[fun together] :: 21/30
Fun indeed. The start is a little fiddly, but once it opens up it's great.

[total] :: 64/90

They move about as fast as rockets (maybe a bit slower), but are more like mines, since they do not go away until they kill the ninja. Because its a menu. Menus are less productive than folders because they use the mouse primarily. You can use the keyboard, just typing in stuff to get places in even Windows Explorer. You can't get to programs however, because they are on the start menu. Unless you happen to be a genius who knows the filename for every .exe you own, which most Windows users don't. What a Mac user could do in 4 keystrokes, a Windows user has to use either 12 keystrokes and know the filename or point and click about 4 times. There's also the hassle if you have more programs than your screen can fill. Its obnoxious. My parents have that, and they can't change the res because they can't see it. Basically, on my keyboard (US), the differences are:
The key left of 1 has a [~ and `]. 2 also has @ on it. I'm not sure what yours has. 3 has # on it rather than the pounds symbol. 4 doesn't have a euro sign.
On the second row of letters (ending in L) I've got the [: and ;] key, and then a [" and '] key. There is a [| and \] key above the enter key and below backspace. There's no Alt Gr, it's just Alt.

#138930 160 2006-02-03T09:17:23Z astro
Quote: Teh Dude, Feb 1 2006, 10:18 PM
Regarding Google Linux being spyware/adware.

First of all, Google is primarily a business. The aim of a business is to make money. Google make money by selling advertising. The niche that Google fills is directed advertising. They decide which adverts to show based on your behaviour. For the search engine, this is simply based on your current query. For Gmail, a bot reads your email and displays adverts based on this.

Google keeps all of your search queries until the year 2038. These search queries are all linked to a unique identifier and your IP address. More recently, they have started to link in further information from your Gmail account (if you have one). Personally, I do not like the idea of a money-driven business having a record of everything that I have searched for, a list of my email contacts and knowledge of the content of my emails.

If you extend still further and get a Google operating system then you really are opening the floodgate to privacy invasion.

Quote: Teh Dude, 2006-02-01T12:48:39Z
Google keeps all of your search queries until the year 2038.
Your 2038 number is just based on the cookies stored on your computer. That's not related to what Google does with the data.

Quote
money-driven business
All businesses are money driven.

Quote: Teh Dude, 2006-02-01T12:48:39Z
Personally, I do not like the idea of a money-driven business having a record of everything that I have searched for, a list of my email contacts and knowledge of the content of my emails.
Deal with it. If you want be a part of the connected world you need to make sacrifices in terms of privacy unless you're going to encrypt all your data. What Google can do with Gmail is no different to what other webmail providers can do. Any site can log your information and any ISP can monitor all your traffic.

Blizzy's chicken salad

1/4 head of lettuce.
1 - 2 Tomatoes.
3 cups chicken, cooked and cubed.
1 1/2 cup celery, sliced.
1/2 teaspoon salt.
1 cup mayonnaise.
2 Tablespoons lemon juice.
1/4 cup onion.
pepper to taste.

Serves 6.

1. Line a medium-sized baking pan with lettuce leaves, and line the edges with half-tomatoes.

2. Mix chicken, celery, salt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and onion in a medium-sized mixing bowl until well-mixed.

3. Pour into baking pan, cover in tin foil. Chill for 30-45 minutes, serve on buns as sandwiches, or as a side dish.

#155574 4 2006-03-18T11:38:45Z astro
It cannot be fixed for a number of reasons. Firstly, the Metanet forum administrator's can't change it because they don't have total control over the forum, only Forumer does. Sigs almost always contain text and sometimes images, so they can't just have you set an image as a sig and nothing else.

This means forumer would need to have their own image hosting service. They would have to use lots of bandwith to host all these sig images, which they probably couldn't afford.

Even if they could, they would have to put a restrictive size limit on the images, which would be a big disadvantage for everyone.

It's so easy to find somewhere reliable to host your images online, so Forumer would never this service anyway.

#165074 28 2006-04-15T15:24:45Z astro
Sweep and Rincewind SW: being the two resident Radiohead megafans, what are you favourite Radiohead albums? I'm curious.

Also, a quick Top Ten from me of my favourite Muse* songs. I tried to write a decent review of each, but I'm truly awful at reviews. So, I've just tried to make a quick statement about each.

10 - Unintended (soft, fairly melancholic)
9 - Cave (nothing astounding, just good overall)
8 - The Small Print (good rock)
7 - Hyper Music (great beat and chorus)
6 - Falling Away With You (quite soft for much of it)
5 - Butterflies and Hurricanes (epic-sounding - two sections, punctuated by a piano interlude)
4 - Time Is Running Out (the catchiest damn verses ever)
3 - Bliss (not sure about this choice, but the arpeggios and main riff is great)
2 - Citizen Erased (epic, 7 minutes long, in four distinct [but still cohesive] sections)
1 - New Born (experimental enough to be interesting without being pretentious]

Honourable mentions:
Plug In Baby (it's all in the riff and the beat)0
Thoughts Of A Dying Atheist (the title alone is enough, but obviously the song is good as well)
Apocalypse Please (not the best song on it's own, but a great opener for the album)
Showbiz (brooding isn't the right word to describe this, but it's similar)
Stockholm Syndrome (just an overall thing)

* Muse being one of my two favourite bands, equal to Franz Ferdinand (for whom I'll do a top ten sometime).

#165801 44 2006-04-17T17:12:25Z astro
As promised, here is my Franz Ferdinand Top 10. It was far easier for me to write comments for this one than on my Muse Top 10.

1. Darts of Pleasure - This is the song that got me hooked on Franz Ferdinand. I can get caught up in the beat so easily, and the whole song just bounces on it. The lyrics are also quite distinctive: you've got "you can feel my lips undress your eyes", and the song ends with three repetitions of a verse in German.
2. You Could Have It So Much Better - A song that is both bright and cynical. I love the lyrics, an inspecific rejection of the accepted order and an equally inspecific call to arms .
3. The Fallen - Lots of biblical allusions in the lyrics that I don't quite get, especially in the breathtaking final chorus.
4. Your Diary - This song doesn't deserve to be a a B-side. The chorus is great (musically, not so much lyrically), and the guitar riffage throughout this song is also excellent.
5. This Fire - Can't really say much about this one. It's... good?
6. Auf Achse - This song is a combination of many different musical stylessort-of-romantic background notes, a disco-y beat, a dance-y beat, and the great choruswhich just manage to form a cohesive song.
This starts off with a romantic sounding intro, and then an almost disco-y beat comes in, giving it a strange vibe. Combined with the chorus, this makes a great song.
7. Take Me Out - A tragically and ridiculously overplayed song, but a fairly good one nevertheless.
8. 40' - It would appear that Franz Ferdinand got writer's block on this song, explaining the two dozen repetitions of "la la la la". A good song nevertheless.
9. Outsiders - Twangy guitars, something that sounds a lot like those weird plastic toy tubes that make a whiny, warbling sound when you turn them upside down, and a drum beat that doesn't change for the entire song.
10. Jacqueline / Eleanor Put Your Boots On - I can't decide. Jacequeline is a more typical song, while Eleanor Put Your Boots On is a much softer song. Call this a tie.

who ever gave this proof gives the best answer mathematically why that is wrong.

2/3 = (exactly equivilent) .666... (repeating)

1/3 + 2/3 = (again, exact) 1
therefore by subsitution:
.333... (repeating) + .666... (repeating) = (exactly, by subsitution) 1

There is no rounding involved and that using one very common mathmatical principal shows .999... = 1

#196231 159 2006-06-29T09:19:36Z astro
But the subsitution is flawed. I think. Lesse...

1/3 is exactly equivalent to .333 recurring infinitely, and 2/3 is exactly equivalent to .666 recurring infinitely. 1/3 + 2/3 = 1, yes. But .333 (rec. inf.) + .666 (rec. inf.) is equal to .999, recurring infintely. After all, 33 + 66 = 99, 3 + 6 = 9, .3 + .6 = .9, so .33 + .66 = .99. No matter how long it recurs, the last digits will still be ...3 + ...6 = ...9.

I see the mathematical subsitution point, but I'm certain it isn't right.

1) There /are/ multiple light sources - Earth, the Sun, and the Moon itself. Think about it. Plus, if it was set up in a studio, do you really think that would have installed multiple lights, or that such an oversight wouldn't've been noticed? Of course not.
2) There's nothing suspiscious about the flag fluttering. The flag was being twisted and moved into position, which will always result in fluttering, regardless of air. In fact, the absence of air means there's little friction, so the flag will keep fluttering more. Also, the flag looks rippled because it was telescopic and it wasn't fully extended. They left it like this because they liked the way it looked. Once again, if it was faked, there would have rectified any issues to do with the fluttering. Plus, since when were movie studios windy?

#213874 3 2006-08-10T08:42:02Z astro
Have a look through online job sites for anything you'd be interested in doing and see what kind of things you'd need. Generally, experience is the main thingfor the things I've looked at in terms of my own future career, anythingrather than degrees.

Also, I don't think it's that important to pick the most useful or widely used programming language when you're starting off learning. The most important thing is understanding the logic and style of programming (whether it be procedural, OOP, etc.). Once you've got good experience with that, you can diversify your programming knowledge, try out different languages, and see the difference. I also don't think formal lessons in programming are that great or useful, but it would all depend on your personal situation.

When it comes to learning languages, find some tutorials if possible, but I find the best resource is normally the official language reference. Books, too, are very good. Go to a library and see if you can find some.

Language-wise, I'd be looking at C, C++, Objective-C, Java, and something like Perl or Python.

Episode One, directly translated into Acceptable English by maestro:
---
The channel of stairs reached down into the cellar of the archaic wooden cabin, obtaining a sense of apprehension that drifted steadily in the dense air. Suspension had consumed the place for over a hundred years, abandoned cobwebs swaying in the moldy corners of every room and closet. The beating wind would not relieve the cabin, as it croaked and moaning with each gust, the rotting wood threatening to break apart. The old legend that belonged to the house was an uncertainty, older than time and changing every occasion it was told. No soul dare mock the tale, no matter how absurd, for fear of being dragged from their beds into the night by some unknown creature that protects the fable, making sure people knew they should not fool with it. Once a majestic palace, it now stands in ruins, defeated by time and nature, without the care of an owner, living or dead. Indeed, someone did once live there, a pathetic, detestable old man who died without a family, buried in the cemetery that lay just beyond the hills to the east near the old military encampment. The mental keenness of his life is still uncertain, as no one wanted to associate with the likes of such a man. It is said that nothing but the airy exist in the darkness of the basements. The unassuming pass by the house from time to time, stopping shortly to ponder what the truth being the myth really was. It was considered a thrusting feat for some, and foolish to others, to even walk past the sagging gate and slam the old iron door-knocker that hung on the door. In fear of angry spirits who wished no visitors, no one stepped inside. Reported to be true to some eye-witnesses, it is said that one day a man accidentally strolled into the residence, and came out but five minutes later spitefully beaten, with bleeding wounds lining his face and chest. Now every time that event is retold, it is looked upon with much vexation, as many believe it to be an unimaginative hoax. Only the pretentious would say that they arent afraid of the cabin, their false courage wiped away when dared to live up to their words and venture into the house. The impassive, dead appearance of the house remains, no matter what people could do to liven it up. Now the large cabin lay abandoned, no one had even walked by it for years. People went on with their lives, no longer unwavering to the tradition of telling the shocking tale of the old man and his home. The doctrine in the ghost stories was unenthusiastic and dull, because no one bothered about it. But something happened that would release all of the legends and tell the truth behind the house. Now we know the true story, and despite our beliefs in the lack of liveliness that lies inside the house, there is always more than meets the eye.
#238123 11 2006-10-07T04:30:38Z astro

---
Under the pretext of daily life, of the regular passing by, no one expected it. The old cabin no longer held the belief of truth it was given as an old legend. Mid morning, Unwanted screams of sheer terror and pain broke the regular solemn, boredom sense that was regular in the old neighborhood. A few brave souls slowly approached the house aggressively, with the slight indication that something wrong, very wrong, just went down. Upon entering the main floor, a sight that would only captivate the likes of R.L. Stine was discovered on the termite-infested wooden floor. The body of a young male was scattered about on the floor, seemingly tossed about like an old rag doll, his head shackled by a thick rope, which stuck out from the ceiling, although cut to let the body fall to the ground.. Fresh blood streamed from dozens of wounds and gashes, staining the carpet a deep deep purplish-red. The fear of the cabin was now permanently fixed into the heart of all society, no longer erratic; it would always be isolated as haunted. But despite the violent and sudden event, it was still up to those willing to prove what really occurred, human or supernatural. It was murder. The rumour of homicide drifted throughout the block, continuing throughout the city. The belief in the inherent superiority of ones own culture that clung to their tradition of superstitions stood on one side, and the frivolous stood on the other, expressing by gesturing about, mocking those who believed in the ghost tale. Truth or tale, it was a true argument among the citizens.

It was having regard to usefulness rather than aesthetics that the feds were brought in. Cops and detectives, professional and lovers of art or science, conspiracy theorists and the scholarly. It was not mysterious that everyone was interested in the case, just because of that fact that the murder was committed in a so called haunted house. Self-contradictorily, those who first severely criticised even the slightest doctrine in the supernatural were now scrambling to solve the death. It may be for the fact that they wanted to slaughter any more nonsense about ghosts and spirits, but it was obvious that they were curious. It was characteristic among neighbors just the same as detectives, as it was finally time to stamp the legends as fact or fiction.

#269323 20 2006-12-13T08:09:32Z astro
The site's mention of W3C standards is misleading. The most important web standard maybe HTML, but the CSS is what most people see, and IE used to have, and to some extent still has, huge problems in that area. Same deal with Acid 2--that's not a test of the most important W3C standards, it's meant to be a very strenuous test: "Acid2 is a complex web page. It uses features that are not in common use yet, because of lack of support, and it crams many tests into one page." Not to mention that that particular 'myth' is quite clearly a joke... even if you cannot infer that, it says quite clearly "this entry was posted on Thursday, June 2nd, 2005 at 1:51 pm and is filed under firefox, greasemonkey, funny."

Basically, I found the content on that 'myths' page to be rather insubstantial and certainly didn't sway me against Firefox. It's considerably biased, just like anything else. Trying to pass it off as 'the fair and balanced truth' as opposed to 'points against Firefox' is misleading.

Either way, I'm down with Opera. I don't normally use it, but it is a good browser. I just use Firefox because it has more features (for me) and I don't generally experience noticable performance issues on my computer.

#13016 1 2006-12-20T12:14:27Z astro
In short, we have strong evidence that says that McP3000 has a second account, Biblios, which he has been using to rate up his own maps. I have gone to considerable lengths to analyse the situation and collect as much evidence as possible; this is absolutely not a rash decision. In fact, if you make any kind of comment to that effect, I'll be rather pissed off. For this McP3000/Biblios case alone there were 4,412 relevant lines in the log. Arachnid may not have had the time to do this kind of thing in the past, but we certainly now do.

So, what evidence, you ask? The following:

The first, most obvious piece of evidence is that Biblios has rated 175 maps, the vast majority of them McP3000's, as '5' over the course of eight and a half months. He has also placed a number of 4 and 4.5 votes, and 16 votes of 0 (mostly for LouDog004's maps; incidentally, this activity started around the time of this post).

For the most part, these votes have come in large sets of votes being made in quick succession.

Votes from the Biblios account have come from two main kinds of IP. These same IP addresses are also used by the McP3000 account, generally immediately before or after Biblios has used them.

Activity on the Biblios account temporarily ceased on 26/10, and did not resume until 05/12. This is quite consistent with a lack of activity from McP3000's account, which slowed down quite a lot around 26/10 and resumed around the 05/10; however, a few votes and a number of logins came from that account, whereas Biblios did not even log in.

As just mentioned, there are two kinds of IP address involved. The first is static, never changing: '63.103.xx.x' (obscured intentionally). The address is only ever used during what would be appropriate times for school. The other kind of IP address changes, but the changes are not large, and it can be reasonably determined that all of these IP addresses are dynamically allocated for a single location. These addresses are used at times that you would not expect to be school hours, ranging up into the early morning.

On a more subjective note, the style of Biblios's maps seems similar to McP3000's, as noted by a popular forumite.

I asked McP3000 whether he knew who Biblios was, and why he would be rating his maps up. McP3000 responded saying that Biblios is a friend from school, and that he knew who McP3000 was, so that would be why he would be rating the maps up. This would be somewhat fair for votes from the 63.103.xx.x IP address, but that does not explain why his friend would be regularly sharing a computer with him (and submitting maps; something that makes this situation more complicated is that Biblios has submitted a number of maps) late at night. I followed up, asking him whether he and Biblios had ever shared a computer elsewhere from which maps would be submitted. He said no.

An exerpt from the logs, only containing relevant details:
Quote
18:58:51-04:00 LOGIN McP3000
19:01:12 VOTE McP3000
19:05:04 VOTE McP3000
19:10:07 VOTE McP3000
19:10:36 LOGIN Biblios
19:11:12 VOTE Biblios
19:11:28 VOTE Biblios
19:11:41 VOTE Biblios
19:11:56 VOTE Biblios
19:12:11 VOTE Biblios
19:12:29 VOTE Biblios
19:12:44 VOTE Biblios
19:13:24 LOGIN McP3000
This shows McP3000 logging in and making three votes. Then, Biblios logs in and makes many votes (5s for McP3000's maps). After this, McP3000 logs back in. This quite clearly shows that only one machine was being used. That one example is not conclusive, but this behaviour has been frequently repeated.

Of course, that conflicts with McP3000's claim that he and Biblios have not shared a computer and used it to submit maps to NUMA. The sheer number of times this has occured means he could not have simply made a mistake in his comment: he was lying. If he was lying about that, there is no reason to think he was telling the truth about who Biblios was.


This evidence is incredibly strong, and a result we will be banning McP for one day for every time he gave a '5' from the Biblios account. 175 days.

Quote: Me a few posts up, 2006-12-22T14:11:57Z
Hmm...I just had an idea, although I don't know why I didn't think of it before...the only reason I can think of is that someone else has already suggested it and I just can't remember now, so if someone already has I'm sorry.

Yeah anyway, I was thinking - why not abolish the 'average rating' system and replace it with a 'most rated' system? Where, instead of calculating an average which can be swayed by snipers, only the rating that has been most chosen for the map would be shown, which would ignore stupid zero's which the map doesn't deserve. This is just another idea to get rid of snipers, by the way, not multi-accounters, I'm just throwing this into the mix. If, at any point, there are two equal most chosen ratings (which would be quite likely, especially when a map is being rated for the first few times), for example if 3 out of 5 and 4 out of 5 are both chosen 15 times, the system could calculate it to be 3.5, for that short period of time when those are equal. I don't know, it's just an idea that I had, and I'm sure I haven't thought it through fully, but I think it could work.
Just wanted to make sure that wasn't ignored...I want to know whether it would work or not.

The mode, in other words. I think the current mean average is the best way to generate a single number to summarise all the ratings.

List! In the earlier years there was little I had to pick from (few albums I knew of) and in the later years there were too many (the last few picks are very contentious to me). I've made note of any other albums that were close to favourite.

1992: R.E.M. - Automatic For The People
There was also Rage Against The Machine - Rage Against The Machine and Pavement - Slanted & Enchanted.

1993: Blur - Modern Life Is Rubbish

1994: Pavement - Crooked Rain, Crooked Rain
There was also Blur - Parklife.

1995: Radiohead - The Bends

1996: Rage Against The Machine - Evil Empire
There was also Beck - Odelay.

1997: Radiohead - OK Computer
There was also Blur - Blur and The Verve - Urban Hymns.

1998: Neutral Milk Hotel - In the Aeroplane Over the Sea

1999: Muse - Showbiz
There was also The Flaming Lips - The Soft Bulletin.

2000: Radiohead - Kid A

2001: Muse - Origin Of Symmetry

2002: Interpol - Turn On The Bright Lights
There was also Muse - Hullabaloo Soundtrack (if that counts) and The Flaming Lips - Yoshimi Battles The Pink Robots.

2003: Muse - Absolution
There was also Radiohead - Hail To The Thief and The Strokes - Room On Fire.

2004: Franz Ferdinand - Franz Ferdinand
There was also Interpol - Antics and Kasabian - Kasabian. And, Soulwax - Any Minute Now.

2005: Arcade Fire - Funeral
There was also Kaiser Chiefs - Employment.

2006: Muse - Black Holes And Revelations
There was also Kasabian - Empire and The Strokes - First Impressions of Earth and... a lot, really. No clear standouts.

This story started there on the fishy dance floor. We were already dancing close, but I wanted even more. There was a limit to what we could do in this public place, so I thought we should find a private space.

"You mean the Chevy Impala from 1965?"
"Yeah, I want to get in it and do a funky jive."
"With your lady friend? Not in my bloody car! I won't clean the upholstery after you 'arrive'."
"It's not like we'll be repopulating the human race--I'm only aiming for second base."

With a reluctant sigh he handed the keys over to me. Now, we could be alone, I realised with glee.

Now, she was a very hot chick, but also more than a little thick. It didn't take much to get her to come to the car, which was parked close by so we didn't need to go far.

I helped her get in to the back seat (she was also drunk, tripping over her feet). "What a fine gentleman you are," she said. "Like a handsome Colonel Sanders covered in tar."

We gazed into each others' eyes; hers were the colour of the night sky. I leant over and kissed her (and hoped to God she wasn't a guy).

There and then I decided that now was the time: go for it, and stop worrying about making your bloody thoughts rhyme!

#316150 11 2007-04-27T06:37:04Z astro
I'd tend to agree with epigone (et al.) that the better maps are being rated the most; now, does the converse apply to all the 0 votes (worse maps also being rated the most)? I wouldn't think so.

As apg said, the overuse of 5s and 0s would be indicative of people voting as if it were a binary yes/no system. That kind of rating behaviour is clearly most common in the 'bronze age' (KA was responsible for defining what most of the ages were). Maps worth 0s or 5s should be very rare, and so a lot of those ratings are basically 'incorrect' by almost any definition, so really the ideal distribution for the ratings should be more focused towards the centre/average and dropping away at the 0s and 5s. That's something that isn't shown on any on the eras--there's always the considerablely sized 0, then the total dropoff and a steady-ish climb towards the higher values.

The average rating over time graph makes me think of the inflation rate. Is it wrong for the average to be above 2.5, or is it valid to say that the majority of NUMA maps are above the 'absolute average' (and if so, what is that 'absolute average' defined by)?

#329490 2 2007-06-10T07:55:12Z astro
Well, you're combining a number of things here. ASCII is a form of character encoding which is used by the computer to convert the letters of the alphabet (and what not) into bits and bytes used internally by the computer. The alt+#### keystroke thing is not based on ASCII encoding numbers. To use the alt numbers, you need to
a) first be using the right numbers
b) be typing them on the numeric keypad
c) make sure num lock is in the right setting.

#329498 4 2007-06-10T09:19:46Z astro
Er, no, that's binary, a number system (that computers do indeed use as the base method of storing everything). Binary is a base-two number system, where as decimal is base-ten. In decimal, each extra digit left is worth ten (hence, base 10) times more than the one to its right (hence, 127 is 7 * 1 + 2 * 10 + 1 * 100); where x is the digit in the 'column' (to use a term) and n is how many places from the right it is (starting at 0), the overall value of the column is x * 10^n (x multiplied by [ten to the power of n]).*.
In binary, each extra digit is worth twice as much as the one to its right, and so you only have two possible numbers: 1 and 0 (hence, 1010 is 0 * 1 + 1 * 2 + 0 * 4 + 1 * 8 = 11 in decimal); the overall value of the column is x * 2^n..

Binary is a useful system for computers and such because it can be stored on anything that has two different states, like on/off, yes/no, pits/lands (in the case of CDs), etc.

I'd suggest that this way of working it out is easier than your mathemetical way: with 01001010, working from the right:

0 * 1 + 1 * 2 + 0 * 4 + 1 * 8 + 0 * 16 + 0 * 32 + 1 * 64 + 0 * 128
= 2 + 8 + 64
= 74



* feel free to ignore the italicised bits, they probably just complicate my explanation

I've stumbled upon a technique I am currently calling 'strip patterns'. Basically, I take an image (like a photograph or a piece of artwork), isolate a strip that is 1px either high or wide and the full size in the other dimension. Then I just expand that out back to the full dimensions, and the result is a striped pattern that generally looks quite cool. They make great wallpapers, and as a bonus they have very small file sizes even at large dimensions.

Audience participation time: give it a shot and comment on the results--or, comment on the fact that you've already done this sort of thing before me.

Quote: Sgt. Poptarts, August 11, 2007 01:34 pm
I was messing with my Video card, and I allowed it to exceed 1024 x 760. Now, it's 1280 x 1024.
Is that a good thing? See, 1024x768 (assuming that's what you meant, or even if it was 760) is a ratio of 1.3 (width divided by height), whereas 1280x1024 is a ratio of 1.25--the appropriate 1.3 resolution is 1280x960. Most CRT monitors have an aspect ratio of 1.3, whereas most (or many) LCD monitors have a ratio of 1.25. The point is, those two resolutions have different aspect ratios, and so assuming you're using the same monitor one of them is going to look somewhat compressed and off.

#369552 29 2007-10-04T05:12:16Z astro
I checked out the Apple website and there's an FAQ page for Garageband that addresses this:
Quote
Using royalty-free loops in GarageBand with commercial work
---
Learn about the usage of royalty-free loops in GarageBand on commercial songs, multimedia presentations, videos, and animations.

The GarageBand software license agreement says:

"GarageBand Software. You may use the Apple and third party audio loop content (Audio Content), contained in or otherwise included with the Apple Software, on a royalty-free basis, to create your own original music compositions or audio projects. You may broadcast and/or distribute your own music compositions or audio projects that were created using the Audio Content, however, individual audio loops may not be commercially or otherwise distributed on a standalone basis, nor may they be repackaged in whole or in part as audio samples, sound effects or music beds."

So don't worry, you can make commercial music with GarageBand, you just can't distribute the loops as loops.

"No-one laughs at Chuck Norris," said Sally, turning towards the rat. "No-one."

#380455 2 2007-11-18T05:08:19Z astro
I would use includes. What you do is put all of the header stuff before the text you want in one file (say, header.php), all of the stuff afterwards in another file (or more than one other file), and then create a new php file that looks something like
include "header.php";
echo "this is the other text stuff you want."
include "theotherstuff.php";
This also has the advantage that, by having all the other stuff in one file, you can make a change and then it will instantly be reflected in all the other files (if this is a good thing for what you're trying to do).

Keeping your teeth clean is quite important. So, you must brush your teeth.

Before we get started, make sure you've got the appropriate equipment:
* Toothbrush
* Toothpaste

Get your toothbrush and squeeze some toothpaste onto it. The ideal amount varies depending on the size of the brush and the strength of the toothpaste.

You can wet the toothbrush before and/or after this process for enhanced effect.

Then, put the toothbrush inside your mouth. Try to make sure your mouth is open wide enough so that you don't accidentally get toothpaste all over your face.

This next step varies, depending on personal choice and whether you're cool and have an electric toothbrush. The basic process of moving the brush around your mouth always applies. If you don't have an electric toothbrush you'll need to manually oscillate the brush at the same time.

Once you feel that you have properly cleaned every part of your mouth, stop brushing and and remove the brush from your mouth.

Now, just spit into a sink and et cetera and you're done!

#385297 9 2007-12-02T06:34:12Z astro
Quote: mattk210, December 02, 2007 04:46 pm
Internet Explorer can display XHTML can't it? my website is XHTML and it displays fine

EDIT: according to the tag on the bottom and the doctype, the w3c site itself is written in valid XHTML, and it works in IE6 and 7
You would be 'serving' your website as .html (text/html) and so all the browsers will interpret it as regular HTML. To be properly parsed as XHTML it needs to be served as XML (application/xhtml+xml) [I'm referring to internet media types]. See the XHTML Media Types document from the W3C: "XHTML documents served as 'text/html' will not be processed as XML [XML10], e.g. well-formedness errors may not be detected by user agents".

Your XHTML may be 'valid', but the code is not necessarily well-formed XML. Either way, IE wouldn't be able to display it as XML.

#385315 11 2007-12-02T08:14:16Z astro
Quote: mattk210, December 02, 2007 06:38 pm
so the w3c itself doesn't use application/xhtml+xml?
Hmm, it doesn't seem to, no. Probably in the interests of compatibility--on that media types page, for example, it's by default XHTML served as HTML, but it has links (under 'this version') for HTML and XHTML (as XML) versions. If you try opening the proper XHTML version in Internet Explorer it fails and asks you to download it instead.

edit: the plot thickens. Their media types summary says that text/html 'may' be used for XHTML 1.0 (HTML compatible). Furthermore,
Quote
The use of 'text/html' for XHTML SHOULD be limited for the purpose of rendering on existing HTML user agents, and SHOULD be limited to [XHTML1] documents which follow the HTML Compatibility Guidelines. In particular, 'text/html' is NOT suitable for XHTML Family document types that adds elements and attributes from foreign namespaces, such as XHTML+MathML [XHTML+MathML].
In other words, they say it's alright (although not explicitly recommended) to serve your XHTML 1.0 as text/html (eg. do what most people are doing with XHTML) so that people with only HTML browsers can view it if you follow the HTML Compatibility Guidelines. However, the Beware of XHTML article does discuss this and says that
a) many people think these compatibility guidelines shouldn't have been made, and
b) XHTML 1.1 removes this provision entirely and states that it should not be sent as text/html.

Quote: Chase, 2007-12-11T15:18:16Z
Hello. Just to forewarn those who haven't recieved it yet, a virus is spreading around Windows Live Messenger users fast! Via the use of .zip files posing as pictures.

Whatever you do, do not save .zip files to your computer via MSN Messenger, Windows Live Messenger, or any IM program you have.

The issue isn't with saving .zips. Firstly, since this isn't to do with an execution vulnerability in Messenger, saving it won't infect your computer. Secondly, opening the .zip won't infect your computer eitherZIPs don't execute (unless you're using a malicious or broken application to open them). According to the article, the .zip contains two files which aren't actually images, but instead a .exe and a .pif. These are what will spread the virus.

I think the real message to take away from this is to be wary of executables (.exe/.pif/.com) and file types you don't recognise.

Also, when you think about it, ".zip" is a funny sounding name.

#390541 6 2007-12-18T05:16:22Z astro
Don't establish the whole plot structure at the start of the book (eg. in Lord of the Rings, Frodo doesn't initially go off with the intent of destroying the ring, he just goes to see the elves). Be sparing with adverbs (eg. said John angrily) and instead try to set the scene with actions and events. Use the active voice (eg. John broke the window, rather than the window was broken by John). Be sparing, creative, interesting. The internet is full of good writing advice, as are good novels.

The Apple Macintosh came out in 1984, years before Microsoft released Office--which did first come out on the Macintosh. This is really of little relevance, though, because (for example) Mirosoft Word was available as a standalone program in 1983, and was available for IBM PCs before it was available on the Macintosh. However, that's still of little relevance, because Microsoft far from pionereed the concept of office-type programs and for a long time wasn't the dominant player--for example, before Word, WordPerfect was the de facto standard; before Excel, there was VisiCalc (a definining application in the history of personal computing). Anyway, my point is that Harley is correct, Windows didn't become more successful than the Mac because they had Word--I'd suggest (and this is where the researched facts stop and my opinion starts) that the fact that Windows was made available to run on hardware produced by anyone, while Apple was the exclusive producer (or, at least, assembler) of everything Mac, had more to do with it (among other factors).

And, of course Apple planned for the Mac to be the most popular operating system in the world, and of course it's all about money, and, er, what reason other than marketing were you suggesting Mac commericals exist for? I'm really not sure what you're getting at. Likewise,

"Mac was made for helping people and other things"

Well, yeah. Of course.

"1. This was made in an era in which people were new to computers. After time, it became useless, but when first introduced, it was a must-have. Bill Gates knew this."

"We long for justice and it is God alone who can offer that justice."
"There is no hope for humanity from within the human race. Our only hope is the God who breaks in from the outside."
This article seems to conveniently skirt around the whole issue that, far from bringing justice, God is letting these genocides and other evil happen. God is omnipotent, and so he could just stop it all. He gave his son Jesus--but he hasn't stopped suffering.

"The God who gives a second Adam."
This hasn't happened yet, right? Why do we need to wait? What possible benefits of waiting could outweight the suffering that currently happens constantly?

"If there is evil in the world how can there not be a God?"
The linked article argues that, without God, evil and suffering would be normal and so wouldn't seem out of the ordinary. I don't follow. "Evil" is just a label for things we consider to be morally despicable. As a label it doesn't require the existence of God. Suffering is the condition of people being in pain or distress. If we are not arguing about creation--and so are not arguing that only God could have created us and made the unpleasant sensation of pain--then I do not see how this argument works. We are not always in serious pain (or suffering greatly), so it is only logical (and not an argument for the existence of God) that we would "cry out for justice" when we do experience, or see/hear people experiencing it.

I'm posting this to help spread the word about the Steal This Film series and the movement it documents. In brief, there are two documentary films in the series, both are a bit more than half an hour in length. They're about BitTorrent, P2P file sharing, and the free culture movement in general.

If you've ever downloaded a copyrighted song or movie from the internet, you have an obligation to watch these. If you have never done this, you also have an obligation. Because I say so. You can download them (for free, of course) through BitTorrent from stealthisfilm.com, or you can watch them streaming on Google Video (#1 and #2).

You will hopefully find these films to be thought-provokingparticularly the second one (so, if you're only going to watch one, let it be that one). If you do watch these films and find yourself seeking more information, you're clearly an intelligent person, and so you can do research on your own. I'd suggest you start by reading Free Culture, a book that's freely available to read online (how fantastic is that!?).

Quote: heatwave21, January 25, 2008 01:54 pm
I say no.
Ever wonder why milk tastes creamy?
I have my doubts about those claims. The raw data are probably true, but they're being sensationalised. Somatic cell count is normally measured in cells per mlif you have a look on the internet, you'll find this is clearly the established standard. I imagine they used a figure of cells per litre on that website so they could have big numbers in the millions. Calling it 'pus' is clearly also an exaggeration. Somatic cell is not an synonym for pus; in fact, in the context of milk production, most of them are white blood cells (leukocytes). Mastitis increases the somatic cell count, but even milk produced by healthy cows has a somatic cell count in the tens of thousands per millilitre. A very low somatic cell count may even be a bad thing:
Quote: http://www.milkproduction.com/Library/Articles/Somatic_Cells_Function_and_Relationship_to_Milk_Production.htm
In part the answer depends on what is considered too low. The key to defending the udder against bacterial challenge is the ability to quickly transfer large numbers of somatic cells to the udder from the circulatory system. Healthy cows tend to have this ability. There is some evidence however that in very low cell count cows, a challenge by bacteria, especially coliforms, may overwhelm the immune system before it can respond and the result can be a very sick animal with clinical mastitis (5).
And, of course, these levels have no meaningful impact upon the creaminess of the milk.

Actually, I don't.
I'm currently working on a song (or, more accurately, an instrumental piece; for now, titled 'Mistyped') and I require assistance. This is a bit outside of the official Metastra compose-perform-edit process; I'm the composer and editor and I'm also doing all the electronic performing.

But what about the other performing? That's where the assistance comes in. I don't play any acoustic instruments, but many of you do, and I'd like you record some stuff for me. As unofficial thing, this is very optional and I'll gladly take whatever I can get.

Especially, though, I'd really like a violin (or other stringed instrument). More than one, even. If you play some other instrument and have some spare time, I'd also love to get whatever you can throw at me (some acoustic guitar could work, for example). Improvisation! It's all good.

Now, I only started composing the piece tonight (although the plan has been in my head for a while), so it's very incomplete. That's okay, because I don't need people to perform the whole thing in one hit. I've got some melodies and notes (and chords, for anyone else playing along) which I'm quite happy with. Once recorded, I intend to chop up, sample, and generally play around with them. I'll have some more recording to ask for when I've finished composing, but we'll get to that when it happens.

By all means give me comments or suggestions, but bear in mind that it's going to be heavily changed (no it is not going to just end like that) no matter what, especially when I can hear everything with recorded instruments.

Now, I can't provide sheet music, but I can offer MP3s of:
* the whole music (with synth instead of strings)
* just the synthesized string parts
* just the backing

and a MIDI of:
* the whole music (very 'interesting' sounding)
* just the string parts

I believe Lenny has a thing that can convert the MIDI into sheet music anyhow. I can also offer the chords and notes themselves, in a not-properly-written-format:

It's in A minor.

Tempo: 125 bpm (ideally).

The main progression is Ami - G, repeating (that's the only chord progression there is at the moment; if you're in an improvisational mood, don't be constrained by that). The first violin plays the root:

A . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . G . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

The melody, played by the other violin (forgive the notation; you should be able to get the rhythm from the provided audio files):

. . E C E . . . . . E C E . . . . . D B D . . . . . D B D . . .


. . E C E . . . . . E C E . . . . . D B D . B . F . E . D . . .

At one point instead of "D B D . B . F . E . D . . ." it goes "D B D . B . F . E . G . . ." for added effect.

I think that's it. Clearly, I know very little about this whole affair, be it the details of playing a violin or telling people how to play something, so tell me if there's anything missing or impractical or whatever here. Also tell your friends.

#428057 6 2008-04-13T15:07:03Z astro
Low denominations of currency have been succesfully removed from a number of countries, including Australia (we got rid of 1c and 2c coins, and also turned our $1 and $2 notes into coins). It's a sensible thing to do when they cost more to produce than they are worth.

It won't have an affect on prices because you round both up and down--1 or 2 goes down to 0, 3/4 goes up to 5, 6/7 < 5, 8/9 > 0. Easy. (And you round the total of the bill, not the individual items, so the effect is always minimal.)

Quote: Strife, April 20, 2008 10:43 am
Quote: maestro, April 19, 2008 02:14 pm
Copyright infringment is not stealing. Downloading a pirated copy does not deprive anyone else of the item. Downloading does not mean someone has a lost a sale. It's not really possible to determine what monetary affect piracy has on sales. Excuse my brevity.
The RIAA gave the figure of 33% expected revenue lost in the music industry as a whole because a number of people who would normally buy the a record simply pirated it instead.

This is exactly what I was talking about when I said you can give your snide "it isn't technically stealing" horseshit instead of realizing the obvious violation of the spirit of the law.
I'm not being snide. It's really nothing like stealing. It's copying. Copying without permission, yes. Illegal in a lot of places (and not just a violation of the 'spirit of the law'), yes. But calling it stealing obscures the issue, which is all about intellectual property, a whole different kettle of fish.

As for the number, anyone can make up a number. I want to know where it comes from. The RIAA says the industry has lost $4.2 billion, but then again, they also claim that every unauthorised download is a lost sale (untrue, through my own experience). There have been other studies made that say the losses are far smaller (to negligible).

This is a bit tangential. I'm not trying to argue piracy should be legalised (not practical), but I am defending some of it. Enough of it to justify my own practices and the continuing availability of the technology, at least.

#435813 39 2008-05-13T15:53:58Z astro
I think I need to explain that my argument isn't trying to offer a concrete proof about God not existing. It's meant to do quite the opposite: demonstrate that the whole issue of the creation of the universe is fundamentally illogical (to us!) regardless of whether you've got a creator God, and that you can't explain things away so simply (or explain them at all, in fact). I suppose it's an argument in favour of strong agnosticism.

Let's say there is a God. He's outside of our universe, our reality, the limits of what we can understand, but if there is a God, he certainly exists.

So, God exists. If something exists, but was never created, then it has always existed. By definition, if nothing created God, he has always existed. This has nothing to do with God existing outside of 'time' and being able to make his own rules. My argument is about our logic. This logic is the only kind we have, it's the only thing we can use to assess and discuss the situation, and it's the only thing that matters here.

All I'm saying is that logically, the idea that God has always existed doesn't make sense. To us. It can't be comprehended. It's like perpetual motion or somethingit goes against all the laws of nature and the universe that we have.

At this point, I'd expect you to be shouting "BUT GOD IS NOT BOUND BY THESE LAWS!". And of course, that's right. I'm not trying to say "science says God can't exist therefore God does not exist, QED". I'm saying God doesn't make sense.

A creatorless universe doesn't make sense either. The universe being created out of nothing? Totally illogical. The universe always existing, having no starting point? Also uncomprehendable.

Obviously, I'm not now trying to say "science says the universe can't exist therefore it does not exist, QED". My argument, if you could call it that, is that, no matter the scenario, the creation of anything and everything, in the universe and beyond, is illogical.

And that's that. Now, here's the (weak) atheistic part that I follow it with: God doesn't make sense, and neither does a creatorless universe. So, to me personally, the idea of God just complicates things (since there's both the universe and God outside of the universe), and so I'm going with the idea that the universe doesn't have a creator.
#435822 41 2008-05-13T16:23:27Z astro
Quote: SkyPanda, 2008-05-13T16:17:17Z
or the creation of the universe isnt bound by human concepts such as time.
I think that's what I'm saying. The whole thing is outside of human concepts and human understanding and so it's not possible to come up with an answer.

Also, it's times like these I wonder why everyone isn't strong agnostic, and so I might as well throw in the other reasoning I have to support this view: If God exists, and he's omnipotent, he will always be able to make it seem like he does not exist. This means we can never prove God does not exist. There is also no way for God to prove to me that he does exist. Every sign could be explained with something else, since there's the possibility that I'm mentally ill and imagining things.

It might just be an indication of how awesome I am at the game, but it took me five minutes to beat that level twice. The only two difficult bits are the jump (between the mines from the diagonal slope with the thwumps) onto the little platform and jumping from the other diagonal slope onto the horizontal with the floorchaser.

With the first bit, don't try to get really close to the gap between the mines and jump vertical. That's tricky. Jump diagonally from behind the gap--behind the mine/gold on the right hand side, even. You could also try jumping off the thwump. For the second jump, make a little jump to get some momentum before going for the horizontal platform.

With regards to creation and the nature and qualia of existence. Religion is about providing an explanation for these things, but it's all still reducible to the same thing: the very concept of existence, of anything existing, is fundamentally beyond logic. I mean, has the universe always existed or was it created from nothing? Has God always existed or was it (He) created from nothing? #444903 103 2008-06-15T15:36:51Z astro
Quote: Atramentis, June 16, 2008 02:05 am
Quote
****. Just, ****

Man, I dont know what to do. ****, oh ****... OH ****ING HELL!!!

Ummm Crap, I dont know how the hell Im supposed to say this. ****, I dont have a ****ing clue. Theres got to be a way to say this properly, but I dont know it. Hell, I didnt ever think that Id ever be signing on to an internet forum to tell its members that one of their most loved members has died.

Im sure you all know Atramentis, or his internet persona, anyway. Brilliant mapmaker, was the top for quite some time, you know the guy? He goes to same school as me, but is in his final year whilst Im still in year 11. We met properly, believe it or not, while playing N He came over, said something like Wow, youre playing N! and then we started talking about stuff like, Have you heard of NUMA?! and so we started talking.

Since then, we got to know eachother quite well He was in the year above me, but we were quite good friends. Wed joke around and stuff, and were trying to arrange a student harvest as his year 12 leaving prank, where wed have this table on the oval, and nothing else, and

No. Enough of that.

I was at school when I got the news. Not the news of his death. He was in intensive care at the time. I was joking around with some of the year 12s he used to hang around with, and there werent a ton of them there, and I asked Wheres Jared? and one of them said in intensive care. You know. I treated it like a ****ing joke, laughed, and asked where he was again. I must have looked like such a ****ing arsehole, ****ing around laughing when there friend was in hospital after getting hit by a car right near his home.

The car driver wasnt even drunk. Or using a mobile phone or anything. There was nothing wrong with her, it wasnt a hit and run or anything, they just ran over who you know as Atramentis on the driveway of a sub divided block. Or maybe there was something mentally wrong with her, I think I heard something of the type mentioned, but screw it, I dont really care about the person who killed Jarred. It couldve been anyone who did the killing, but its the death that screwed me over.

He was wearing headphones on high volume, and thatd be the lesson of the death, insofar as there is one, dont wear headphones in traffic, but it wasnt in traffic and it there isnt a lesson to be learnt here, just a bloody pointless waste of life.

And, again, I dont bloody know how to say this, but hes dead. He was in intensive care for, I think, 18 hours or so. He died with his family at his side, but hell, what difference does that make? Hes still dead. He still died. In a charmless hospital room with machines pumping stuff in and out of him

Hell. What do I know of that? I wasnt there. I didnt see it. And Im sort of grateful for that. I dont want to have the memory of a last rattled breath, or of the slight, almost undetectable switch from tortured living to the nothingness of death no, who needs the memories of such things? The imagination of it is bad enough.

I only recently heard that hes dead. Full on dead. Not lying down someplace slowly recovering, to emerge not unchanged but ALIVE, damnit, and still the same person in some deep down place And thats that. A brilliant man lost to the world from

Oh, damnit, I sound like Im delivering a Eulogy or something. Plenty of time for that later, when a real one does get delivered over what used to be Jarred. Probably delivered by a priest or something, who never knew of his convoluted, partially atheist but GOOD views on religion. I prayed for him, can you imagine that? I dont even have a clue if he wouldve wanted me to or not, but I did all the same, and I never wouldve thought it

Crap. I really dont know what to do, what to say, what to write, what to tell my family when at long last they come home (though they never even met him, and only supplied transport to his house grudgingly when they had nothing better to do), and well, here I am. On the frigging internet, telling a frigging bunch of zit- covered prepubescents about the death of someone they know nothing about, somebody who theyll never feel the actual zest of loss for anymore than they would somebody like Brickman who just, one day, disappears. Hell, to you, he could still be alive someplace and well for all you know, and so it wont be real.

I only wish I had that.

So yeah, thats it. He died, I didnt even hear about it until it was almost over, and now hes being shoved into the ground like so much garbage in an expensive case in just a few days time. No, if you live nearby, youre frigging not allowed to drop in and pay your respects during the service like some sort of retarded, messed up gatecrasher.

And here I am, going to watch my third generic, fill-the-blanks eulogy from some uninspired priest, and see my third body swallowed by the earth, and wish it wasnt so. Violently, violently wish it wasnt so.

The world has just experienced a great loss. Just another great loss, and they happen all the time, but this shouldnt have been. Im sorry.

And thats it. Im done.

Bye.

Quote: _destiny^-, June 17, 2008 12:04 am
christianity was in my mind, most other religons have some other name for 'god'
Just wondering since you didn't capitalize "god." I could say that everything happens for a reason and that God knows, what he's doing, but I don't know. First you have to keep in mind that, in Christianity, noone is truly "innocent." Since Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit, everybody, except of course Jesus, has been a sinner. But I am on your side in that it's bullcrap what happens to some people. I'm 14 and my mom's dead. She was 36. One of my best friends is 19 and already has skin and lung cancer. Did God do this? Let me first say that my mom died at such a young age because she abused drugs and alcohol to the point to where she couldn't stop. Did God plan that? Valerie, my afore-mentioned friend, has skin cancer because she didn't wear sunblock and has lung cancer because she smokes. Even after she was diagnosed. Is this God's doing? I say no. But what about me? I was hurt because of my mom's stupid decisions that lead to her death last summer. Why did God let that happen?

God didn't do that. God has nothing to do with anything bad that's is happening in the world right now. As the people at my church say, "God is good, all the time." People are hurt because of the decisions they make and the consequences that ripple outward, affecting everyone around them.

But what about things you can't help at all? Like a loved one dying in a car crash?

I don't know. Life is bullcrap sometimes.
When you're the all-powerful, all-knowing, and apparently all-loving God of the universe, it's absolutely your responsibility.

You mentioned free will, which must be an incredibly important thing, since God allows massive atrocities to occur because of it. But waitGod is known for divine intervention. The Bible, in both the Old and New Testament, records Him directly interfering with affairs on Earth and causing miracles. To be canonised you have to perform two miracles. So it's obviously not that importantif you have enough faith, you can do all kinds of miraculous things.

But why should faith matter? If God is totally good, He would want there to be less suffering the world. There may be conditions on that, but that's got to be the ultimate goal. Otherwise, it's a nonsense definition of benevolence.

Let's assume one of the conditions is free will. God wants there to be less suffering in the world, but He refuses to do anything that interferes with free will. No-one can know that anything out-of-the-ordinary has happened. There are still things He could do.

Take SIDS, for example. Innocent babies dying in their sleep. God has the power to intervene and stop this from happening. He wouldn't lose any of his mystique if he stopped this from happening. No-one would suspect a thing. There would just be less suffering in the world. All kinds of other medical conditions could be averted without interfering with free will, and also genetic disorders. It isn't anyone's choice to have haemophilia. Or HIV/AIDS. If God wanted less people to die and less people to suffer, He could absolutely do it, without affecting anything else.

#448488 21 2008-06-25T09:09:50Z astro
Nah, there's no good reason to bring back bitesizing. It was just an arbitrary layer of elitism, in that people were given the power to anonymously say a map is really good without further justification. Many users were complaining about poor quality maps being bitesized. So, it was improved, and now we've got featured maps, which is much better. There's now accountability and transparencyinstead of appointing people on the grounds that they've got better taste than the commoners, we're giving it to people who have demonstrated they can write good reviews and justify their opinions.

Bitesizing could return and run parallel with featured maps, but what would the point be? I imagine bitesizing was thought to be better because it was easier to promote a mapbut that's not an inherently good thing. As I said, poor maps were being bitesized andmost importantlythey were being promoted without any justification.

For instance - one of the reasons Guns and Roses' guitar players (Slash & Izzy) were so notable is because of the way Izzy's rythym and atmosphere suited Slash's searing leads perfectly.


You can't just stick a bunch of people in there - think about it. If you wanted to make the best cookie - you would probably add the best ingredients, right? Think, I'll add chocolate, vanilla, strawberry, sugar, otmeal rasin, peanut butter and all the best flavors. They're good on their own - mixed with complementing things such as flour, or butter - but together - they are a disaster. Put some thinking into it.

And technically I don't think we have the technology to create Ad's band but it's still fun to think about.

(Wikipedia:

Weak agnosticism, or empirical agnosticism (also negative agnosticism), is the belief that the existence or nonexistence of deities is currently unknown but is not necessarily unknowable and therefore one should withhold judgment until/if more evidence is available.

Strong atheism is a term generally used to describe atheists who accept as true the proposition, "gods do not exist". Weak atheism refers to any other type of non-theism. Historically, the terms positive and negative atheism have been used for this distinction, where "positive" atheism refers to the specific belief that gods do not exist, and "negative" atheism refers merely to an absence of belief in gods.)
